# Independent precise-rung confirmation review

The frozen N01–N06 keyless comparison completed once under the separately committed authorization amendment. Its [sealed output receipt](novelty-precise-rung-01c2c-sealed-output-receipt-2026-09-26.json) pins the result, blind packet, and lifecycle bytes. All 12 calls completed with 26 trace-verified ESearch rungs and 108 metadata IDs; the exact underlying wire-request count is unknown. The driver removed both child processes and isolated worktrees. No product model call, paid fallback, or retry occurred in the retrieval run.

The 36-item [blind packet](novelty-precise-rung-01c1-confirmatory-blind-2026-09-25.json) was reviewed from a separate packet-only temporary directory by Antigravity Gemini 3.8 Flash High. The complete [labels](novelty-precise-rung-01c1-confirmatory-blind-labels-2026-09-25.json) were committed at `37ac42b8` before the scoring key, PMIDs, or arms were inspected. All 36 labels are evaluable; none is `insufficient_abstract`.

The deterministic [score](novelty-precise-rung-01c1-confirmatory-score-2026-09-26.json) gives positive-target PMID recall@3 of **0/3 baseline and 0/3 candidate**. The candidate loses no positive target or distinct control anchor and increases the unrelated count on no request, but it fails the preregistered strict primary improvement gate. An independent Antigravity high-effort scoring audit recomputed the positive targets, controls, per-request unrelated counts and label completeness and found no mismatch. The prior exploratory comparison passed its own gate, but the frozen joint rule requires both comparisons to pass. This complete, provenance-valid confirmation therefore **rejects adoption of the isolated precise-rung candidate**. The result is limited to the six frozen queries across three domains; it does not establish a general PubMed ranking or scientific-quality result.

No candidate runtime code was merged into the product and no deployment is warranted for this rejected adaptation. The isolated candidate, runner and receipts remain retained as reproducible evidence rather than a runtime dependency.
